scenario: AITA for reducing my tip to compensate for a drink I didn’t order? (US) | So short story, at a restaurant today for lunch I got an entree and a glass of water (not fancy water mind you, just tap and it didn’t even have ice). My girlfriend got the same entree and a tea. When the cheque came we had been charged the same amount, $10 for the entree and $2 for a “beverage”. When I pointed this out to the waitress she said water was a beverage and I needed to pay for it. When it came time to tip time I did the math for what I would usually tip, $2.50 tip for my $10 entree and then subtracted the price of the $2 tap water. Basically I left a .50 cent tip. My girlfriend thinks it was an asshole move and I think I’m not paying $2 for lukewarm tap water. basically I brought my cheque total to the $12.50 it would have originally been without the water added.

prediction.raw: I would say: 1 (You are the asshole). Here's why: while it's understandable that you felt frustrated about being charged for tap water, reducing your tip to compensate for the drink you didn't order is not the right approach. The tip is intended to show appreciation for the server's service, not to punish them for a perceived mistake on the bill. By subtracting the cost of the water from your tip, you're essentially penalizing the server for something that may not have been their fault. It's possible that the restaurant's policy is to charge for water, and the server was simply following procedure. A better approach would have been to politely speak with the server or manager about the issue and ask them to remove the charge for the water. This way, you can address the problem directly and avoid affecting the server's tip, which is a significant part of their income. Additionally, leaving a tip of only $0.50 on a $10 entree is a very low tip, even if you were trying to make a point. This could be seen as unfair to the server, who may have provided good service despite the mistake on the bill.
